course.summary: Force, pressure and friction explained through things you can try at home.

skills.name: Describe force as a push or pull and its effects
Relate pressure to force and area
Explain what friction is and what it depends on
Choose ways to increase or reduce friction

lessons.title: Force: a push or a pull

sections.heading: What is a force?
sections.text: A **force** is a push or a pull on an object. Kicking a football is a push; opening a drawer is a pull.

sections.heading: What a force can do
sections.text: A force can start or stop motion, change speed or direction, and change the shape of an object, like squeezing a ball of dough.

sections.heading: Measuring force
sections.text: Force is measured in **newtons (N)**. When two forces act in opposite directions, the net force is their difference.

questions.stem: Which is an example of a pull?
questions.explanation: Opening a drawer draws it towards you: a pull.
hints: Which one moves the object towards you?

questions.stem: What is the SI unit of force?
hints: Named after the scientist of the laws of motion.

misconceptions.1: The pascal is the unit of pressure.

questions.stem: Two teams pull a rope with 300 N and 250 N in opposite directions. Net force?
questions.explanation: Opposite forces subtract: 300 − 250 = 50 N, towards the stronger side.

misconceptions.0: Forces in opposite directions don't add up.

questions.stem: Squeezing a lump of clay mainly shows that force can…

sections.heading: Force on an area
sections.text: **Pressure = force ÷ area.** The same force on a smaller area gives more pressure.

sections.heading: Everyday examples
sections.text: A sharp knife cuts easily because its thin edge has a tiny area. School bags have wide straps so the weight spreads over a bigger area and presses less on the shoulders.

sections.heading: Units
sections.text: Pressure is measured in **pascals (Pa)**: 1 Pa = 1 N per square metre.

questions.stem: A 100 N force acts on 2 m². What is the pressure?
Why do camels walk easily on sand?
options: Their broad feet spread weight over a larger area
questions.explanation: Larger area means less pressure, so they sink less.

questions.stem: If the area is halved and the force stays the same, pressure…
questions.explanation: Dividing by half the area doubles the result.
hints: Try force 10 N on area 2 then area 1.

misconceptions.0: Pressure goes the opposite way to area.

questions.stem: The SI unit of pressure is…

misconceptions.0: The newton is the unit of force.

sections.heading: A force that opposes motion
sections.text: **Friction** acts between two surfaces in contact and opposes their relative motion. A ball rolling on the ground slows down because of friction.

sections.heading: Why it happens
sections.text: Even smooth-looking surfaces have tiny bumps. The bumps of the two surfaces catch on each other.

sections.heading: What it depends on
sections.text: Friction is larger for rougher surfaces and when the surfaces are pressed together harder.

options: opposite to the direction of motion
hints: Why does a rolling ball slow down?

questions.stem: On which surface will a marble roll the farthest?
questions.explanation: The smoothest surface has the least friction.

hints: Look closely at a surface under a magnifier.

questions.stem: Pressing two surfaces together harder makes friction…
hints: Try rubbing your palms softly, then hard.

sections.heading: When we want more
sections.text: Treads on shoes and tyres increase friction so we don't slip. Gymnasts put powder on their hands for a better grip.

sections.heading: When we want less
sections.text: Oil and grease (lubricants) reduce friction between moving machine parts. Ball bearings replace sliding with rolling, which has much less friction.

sections.heading: A necessary evil
sections.text: Friction wastes energy as heat and wears things out, but without it we could not walk, write or hold anything.

questions.stem: Why are ball bearings used in machines?
options: To replace sliding with rolling and reduce friction
questions.explanation: Rolling friction is smaller than sliding friction.

questions.stem: Friction is called a 'necessary evil' because…
options: it is useful but also wastes energy
questions.explanation: We need it to walk and grip, but it causes wear and heat.
hints: Think of both good and bad effects.

questions.stem: Gymnasts rub powder on their hands to…
questions.explanation: The powder absorbs sweat and improves grip.
hints: They must not slip off the bar.
